In a scenario-based visual survey, 62 respondents rated short AI-generated animations contrasting robot behaviors in five office scenarios and evaluated technical and socio-psychological attributes. The largest differences between depicted conditions occurred in the security-gate and level-change scenarios, and close passing markedly lowered evaluations; respondents’ sensitivity to these differences was not associated with acceptance. Technical evaluations were strongly associated with socio-psychological evaluations and had a significant total association with acceptance, and socio-psychological evaluations were positively associated with acceptance at the 10% level. Mediation was not supported. A positive technical × socio-psychological interaction suggests that the association between technical evaluations and acceptance became more positive as socio-psychological evaluations increased, although none of the simple slopes was individually significant. The results suggest that respondents were sensitive to how robots handled building features and provide preliminary evidence for robot-friendly office design and service design.

paper_title: A Survey of AI Virtual Cells: Representation Learning, Perturbation Prediction, and Intervention Design
paper_abstract: Predicting cellular responses to genetic and chemical interventions supports disease research and therapeutic discovery. Experimental screening is costly, limiting coverage of interventions and cellular contexts. This survey reviews artificial intelligence virtual cells (AIVC) through the progression from state representation learning to perturbation prediction and intervention design. We describe how state representations support response modeling and how learned responses guide intervention selection across previously untested interventions and diverse cellular contexts. We summarize data resources, representative model families, evaluation strategies, and multimodal, temporal, and spatial extensions, then discuss generalization and experimental feedback. A curated resource collection is available at https://github.com/ttruan2426-dot/Awesome-Single-Cell-Perturbation-Prediction.

paper_title: A Technique to Model Product Information and User Reviews (MPIUR)
paper_abstract: Modern e-commerce platforms naturally provide three complementary modalities: textual item descriptions, item images, and user reviews. However, existing multimodal recommendation methods often omit reviews or do not integrate all three modalities within a unified framework. In this paper, we propose MPIUR, a multimodal graph-based recommendation model that encodes reviews in heterogeneous graphs, aligns image and text representations, and adapts collaborative--semantic alignment to item interaction density. Experiments on the Amazon Reviews 2023 Musical Instruments and Baby categories show that MPIUR achieves the best global nDCG@10 and Recall@10 among the evaluated methods on both datasets. It also obtains the best nDCG@10 and Recall@10 on sparse items, indicating that jointly exploiting reviews and multimodal item content is particularly useful when interaction histories are limited.

paper_title: Counting Under Disagreement: Dollar-Weighted Measurement, Selective Machine Labelling and Budgeted Human Review from Disagreeing AI Readers of Administrative Text
paper_abstract: We study AI-assisted measurement when one text label applies to many administrative records, the target is a monetary total, and the human readings that anchor the machines disagree. The testbed is 121,070 grant-purpose texts from US tax filings (799,675 records, \$126.4B), labelled by a rule-based classifier and three language models, with a designed sample of 651 texts read independently by three people under one codebook. We state exact conditions for a fixed-predictor difference estimator and for a cross-fitted predictor whose folds are assigned to the whole frame before sampling, under Poisson sampling, and assess the implemented fixed-size procedures by simulation: 8 predictors whose own totals span \$11.2-15.0B agree to within \$0.4B once rectified. Two rules that accept machine labels at a stated dollar-weighted error, weighted conformal p-values under a dollar measure and Learn-then-Test on the design estimate of the error, are evaluated on nested held-out folds and on re-draws of the design with synthetic truths; their error control in deployment is not established, and the count-based rule accepts no text under a dollar-drawn sample. In a replay that charges every human label, a two-phase review policy whose calibrator is fitted on its own first phase reduces the RMSE of the total by 28% at a budget of 100 texts relative to dollar-proportional sampling, while pure Neyman allocation fails with an uncalibrated predictor. Independent readers shift the estimated total by \$3.93B, 2.2 times the within-reader sampling interval, and institution-level intervals under-cover at every size. Every headline result is re-run under each reader. The results identify both the benefits and the limits of using learned predictions to decide what a person should verify.
comments: 61 pages, 8 figures, 46 tables. Replication record (calibration sample, population aggregates, prompts and analysis code): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23285230

paper_title: Multimodal Judges Flag, Humans Decide: A Review-and-Edit Framework for AI-Generated Product Video Ads
paper_abstract: Generative pipelines can now turn every product page of an e-commerce catalog into a short video ad, but deciding whether such an ad is usable is not one good-or-bad call. We describe how we operationalized the review and editing of these ads so that both can keep pace with generation: reviewers go through each ad scene by scene and answer six questions, on the product, scene quality, pronunciation, script, sound and captions; judges built from vision-language, speech and language models file each finding under the matching question, and reviewers accept or reject each finding and add what the judges missed. Each confirmed issue then opens an edit tool matched to it. The questions and the routing from a finding to its fix do not depend on the models that generate the ad. Across 120 ads from our pipeline, reviewed with judge findings on screen, reviewers marked the product wrong on 60% of scenes, and script, caption or sound problems on under 10% each. On 60 of these ads, they marked the product wrong on 58% of scenes, far more than the 26% marked by two reviewers who later saw the ads with the judges hidden; one reviewer who saw the ads both ways marked 57% with judge findings and 19% without. On 120 blind-labeled scenes, a product judge that watches the clip with the catalog photos reached AUC 0.84, while video-quality and photo-similarity scores were close to chance. We tune the judges for recall: the product judge catches nearly all defects but also flags many clean scenes, so reviewers decide; together, the judges widen what reviewers mark and reviewers add what the judges miss. Without judge findings, one reviewer's marking faded over a session. We release a review-portal template and our review data (120 ads and 562 scenes with judge findings and human marks, plus 120 blind-labeled scenes with baseline scores) at https://github.com/anoubhav/ad-review-and-edit.
comments: Accepted at the WVAQ workshop at WACV 2027

paper_title: Clinical predictions using artificial intelligence in neurosurgery and its subspecialties: a systematic review and meta-analysis
paper_abstract: Artificial intelligence models for clinical prediction are proliferating across neurosurgery, but their aggregate discriminative performance, distribution along the care pathway and methodological quality are unclear. We systematically reviewed and meta-analysed these studies in neurosurgery and its subspecialities along with their risk of bias appraisal. We performed a PRISMA search for peer-reviewed original studies using AI to predict a clinical outcome in neurosurgical populations. Metrics were pooled using random effects modelling. Each study was classified as diagnostic, prognostic or forecasting and was assigned an evidence level. Clinical prediction task sub-stratification analysis was performed. Risk-of-bias was assessed using PROBAST. 1063 studies were included. Across 451 studies reporting AUC, pooled discrimination was 0.86, ranging from 0.84 (spine) to 0.87 (neuro-oncology), with extreme heterogeneity. Performance varied by clinical pathway stage, highest for diagnosis, grading and molecular tasks and lowest for post-operative tasks. Only 51 studies were using prospective data with external validation, whereas 619 rested on internal validation alone or no validation. 89 percent studies were at high risk-of-bias, driven by the analysis domain. AI models report high performance across all the neurosurgical subspecialities, concordant across AUC, accuracy, sensitivity and specificity and robust to risk-of-bias stratification. Performance is highest for imaging-anchored diagnostic tasks and lowest at decision-facing post-operative stage. However, the literature is dominated by optimism-prone, internally-validated and poorly calibrated models with extreme heterogeneity. External validation, calibration analysis and reporting guidelines adherence remain prerequisites for clinical adoption.

paper_title: PARIS: A multi-agent LLM framework for end-to-end, PRISMA-guided systematic literature reviews with pre-synthesis corpus quality assessment
paper_abstract: Systematic literature reviews (SRs) remain slow and labor-intensive, and most automation tools address single stages of the workflow. We present PARIS (PRISMA Agentic Research Intelligence System), an open-source framework in which a conductor agent running in Claude Code orchestrates 15 specialized large language model (LLM) agents, from scoping a research question to exporting a manuscript draft. Agents are specified declaratively, coordinate exclusively through persisted artifacts that the conductor validates before every transition, and delegate retrieval, bibliometric analysis and scoring to deterministic Python utilities. Three human checkpoints gate study inclusion, corpus adequacy and the synthesis outline. We also introduce QualityScore, a pre-synthesis index that aggregates normalized network, bibliometric, semantic and process sub-scores into a 0-100 grade. Two case studies illustrate both: AI chatbots and university students' learning (388 records, 100 included) and AI-assisted SR methods (131 records, 123 included, QualityScore 69.1 recomputed with a proxy network sub-score). They show end-to-end feasibility across domains and the diagnostic use of QualityScore: in the first run, corpus improvements chosen at the corpus-adequacy checkpoint raised the score from 74.6 to 81.9 and the number of pre-2023 studies from 1 to 19. Audits of both runs exposed failure modes: incomplete retrieval, counts that drifted between agents, unrecorded or delegated checkpoint decisions and a grade that depends on how citation data are handled. PARIS fully supports 8 of the 27 PRISMA 2020 items and partially supports 11. Output quality has so far been judged only by an internal reviewer agent; independent validation against human reviews is the next step.

paper_title: Next-Generation Segmentation in Radiotherapy: A Narrative Review from Atlas-Based Methods to Agentic Vision-Language Models
paper_abstract: Precise segmentation of target volumes and organs at risk is an essential prerequisite for modern, high-precision radiation therapy. However, this task has traditionally been time-consuming and subject to high interobserver variability. Motivated by these limitations, more advanced and novel approaches to automating this task have been developed over the past two decades. This narrative review highlights representative milestones, with a focus on the most recent developments. These approaches include atlas-based label propagation, convolutional architectures, promptable foundation models, and, most recently, vision-language models (VLMs), which integrate clinical text with volumetric segmentation. Each methodological generation has addressed limitations of its predecessor while introducing new ones. A substantial gap remains between research progress and clinical deployment, as routine workflows continue to be dominated by atlas-based and narrow task-specific deep-learning tools, which remain strong baselines in geometric overlap metrics but are highly rigid in terms of application, versatility, portability, and interpretability. As contouring systems further grow in complexity, conventional geometric overlap metrics become insufficient, motivating evaluation paradigms that incorporate surface-based, dosimetric, and prompt-adherence assessment. Emerging agentic architectures that combine large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, and vision-language segmentation modules are leading towards more flexible, guideline-aware, interactive contouring workflows. These systems could automate flexible and interpretable knowledge-based contouring and actively support the clinical reasoning underlying target volume definition.

paper_title: Trajectory Density Ratios under Weak Support: A Survey across the Sciences
paper_abstract: Many problems across the sciences compare two stochastic processes through the sequences they generate. Reinforcement learning asks what a new policy would return from the trajectories of an old one; molecular simulation asks how much more a ligand binds from samples of the unbound state; climate attribution asks how a heat wave shifted under warming; and language-model post-training asks what a deployed agent will do from logged interactions. In every case, one quantity would answer all these questions at once: the ratio of the two probability laws over their generated sequences, the trajectory density ratio. This ratio exists only under strong conditions. When one process reaches states the other cannot, the ratio does not exist; when their overlap is thin, its variance grows without control with the sequence length; and when they concentrate on different lower-dimensional sets, the ratio is undefined altogether. Weak support of this kind is the norm for sequence data, not a sampling accident, and its price is paid in identifiability rather than in noise alone. This survey organizes the field around a three-level diagnosis of weak support and a map of the nine retreats that methods take when the full ratio is out of reach, from direct estimation and reweighting through staged decomposition, stationarization, and partial-identification bounds to smoothing, transport couplings, operator spectra, and direct estimation of a single functional. Each retreat keeps part of what the ratio offers and pays for the rest, and each application domain has standardized the retreat its data force. The survey closes with open problems: testable diagnostics at every level, partial identification at the trajectory level, a rate theory of time-amplified error, and benchmarks with ground truth.

paper_title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
paper_abstract: Recent studies of embodied agents based on frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs) develop harness engineering around the MLLM, such as harnesses with post-trained policies and recursive self-improvement loops. Yet whether these additions exceed the native capability of the MLLM remains unexplored. We introduce SimplEvo to explore how far an MLLM can improve under direct control when it retains its execution experience in self-written text memories. It requires no weight updates, post-trained policies, or privileged information. The MLLM writes a coordinate-free task memory once from a single demonstration. Under a strict train-test protocol, it then creates a bounded working memory on training episodes only and refines it after each episode with lessons on procedure, completion, and recovery. Both memories stay fixed at test time. On EBench, SimplEvo lifts the success rate (SR) of GPT-6-Astra under direct control from 46.7% to 81.7%, and tops the RoboDojo leaderboard with 69.63% SR and a score of 75.32. Compared with memories that also store past visual frames, SimplEvo reaches a similar SR with text memory alone while using fewer tokens. With its memories fixed, SimplEvo also generalizes to unseen layouts and randomized scene configurations. Moreover, the working memory transfers across models: written by GPT-6-Astra, it can be reused as is by weaker MLLMs and improve their performance without any adaptation of their own.

paper_title: Multimodal Graph Learning: A Survey of Models, Benchmarks, and Frontiers
paper_abstract: Multimodal attributed graphs (MAGs), in which nodes carry text, images, and other modalities while edges encode relations among entities, underlie e-commerce, social media, content platforms, and creative applications. Learning on MAGs has developed along two complementary lines: graph-centric methods redesign how modalities are fused, propagated, and connected within message passing, while foundation-model-centric methods pretrain transferable multimodal graph encoders or bring graph context into multimodal large language models for prediction and generation. In parallel, several benchmarks have appeared with different datasets and evaluation protocols. This survey takes an algorithm-centric and evaluation-grounded view of the field and makes three contributions. Modeling: we introduce a unified message-passing formulation and organize methods into five integration levels (feature, propagation, topology, learning, and foundation model), covering discriminative and graph-conditioned generative models; within this formulation we derive representative methods as special cases, compare their assumptions, expressiveness, and cost, and identify cross-modal sensitivity as a property that separates otherwise similar architectures. Datasets and evaluation: we review recent benchmarks, summarize their datasets and metrics, define model-independent descriptors (label homophily, average degree, clustering, and edge provenance), and map each evaluation protocol to the baselines it uses. Frontiers: we connect multimodal graph learning to AI agents, covering the multimodal graphs that agents perceive and remember and graph engineering, the practice of organizing agent workflows as explicit graphs; we then discuss open problems, concrete efforts for the community, and research directions, including when graph structure helps in the presence of strong multimodal foundation models.

paper_title: Where Subsidized Housing Lands, and Why It Matters: A Review of LIHTC Siting, Neighborhood Opportunity, and Fair Housing
paper_abstract: The Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) is the main federal tool for producing affordable rental housing in the United States. Because its units are fixed in place for decades, each siting decision shapes the neighborhoods available to many successive low-income households. This review connects three bodies of research that are usually read separately: studies of where LIHTC developments are located, studies of how neighborhoods affect the long-run outcomes of the people who live in them, and studies of how LIHTC projects change the neighborhoods that receive them. We first describe how the program's design builds location choices into every allocation, and then organize the evidence around four questions: where projects go, why they go there, what location means for tenants, and what it means for existing residents. LIHTC properties remain clustered in higher-poverty, higher-minority areas. That clustering reflects land and construction markets, zoning, local opposition, and allocation rules as much as tenant demand. Neighborhood exposure has large effects on children's adult outcomes, yet LIHTC investment can also raise property values, reduce crime, and improve conditions in distressed neighborhoods, while its effects in higher-income areas are neutral or negative. The result is a genuine trade-off between expanding tenants' access to opportunity and reinvesting in disinvested places, and its terms vary with local context. We close by mapping policy levers to each part of the siting decision and by setting out a research agenda centered on causal identification, tenant-level outcomes, and within-city variation.

paper_title: Neuroimaging Correlates of Distinct Phenomenological Subtypes of Auditory Verbal Hallucinations in Schizophrenia: A Critical Review of fMRI and Structural Connectivity Evidence
paper_abstract: Auditory verbal hallucinations (AVH) affect most people with schizophrenia and persist in a substantial minority despite adequate antipsychotic treatment, including clozapine. Three decades of neuroimaging have nonetheless failed to converge on a single neural substrate. This critical review tests the hypothesis that this inconsistency partly reflects unmodelled phenomenological heterogeneity. We synthesised functional MRI and structural/diffusion connectivity studies of AVH in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders, separated hallucination-state from trait designs, and mapped each finding onto empirically derived phenomenological subtypes using three explicit evidence tiers. State studies converge on speech-production and speech-perception systems, with left inferior frontal and right middle temporal activation preceding onset by 6–9 s, whereas trait studies converge on reduced left superior and middle temporal engagement. Arcuate fasciculus findings diverge by metric and segment: anisotropy and magnetisation transfer increase in whole-tract studies, decrease in segment-resolved analyses, and tract length rises with severity. Provisional subtype-specific signals emerge: parahippocampal deactivation before memory-replay experiences; right inferior frontal lateralisation tracking negative valence in low-complexity, commanding voices; reduced temporal-to-frontal effective connectivity in inner-speech-type hallucinations; and associative rather than primary auditory generators in deafferentation-related hallucinosis. Direct imaging comparisons within phenomenologically defined subtypes remain almost entirely absent. We propose a subtype–substrate framework and a research programme combining structured phenomenology, within-subject state and trait acquisition, segment-resolved diffusion modelling and stratified neuromodulation as the most tractable route to resolving the field’s inconsistencies and to mechanism-targeted treatment.

paper_title: Clinical, Immunological, Biochemical and Safety Outcomes of Eryxin (Reptilin) in Human Studies: A Systematic Review of Published and Grey Literature
paper_abstract: Background. Eryxin (Reptilin), an aqueous snake autolysate developed in Uzbekistan, has been used since the 1990s as an immunomodulating agent. Its clinical evidence is dispersed across published and grey literature.Objective. To identify and appraise human studies of Eryxin or Reptilin and summarise their clinical, immunological, biochemical and safety outcomes.Methods. We searched PubMed, Europe PMC, Google Scholar, eLIBRARY.ru, CyberLeninka, three trial registries, libraries and archives; the last search update was on 30 September 2026. Human studies of any design with extractable data were eligible. Authors independently extracted data with artificial-intelligence assistance; discrepancies were checked against original scans. Two reviewer pairs independently assessed risk of bias for prioritised outcomes using the 2016 Risk Of Bias In Non-randomised Studies of Interventions tool for controlled studies and the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute before–after tool for uncontrolled studies. Synthesis was descriptive without meta-analysis. Certainty was summarised by condition and for adverse events using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach.Results. Twenty-two non-randomised studies across 16 conditions were included (64 reports), all conducted in Uzbekistan. A reliable total number of unique participants was unavailable because of uncertain cohort overlap and inconsistent participant counts. Most reports were retrieved from libraries and archives. Eleven of 16 controlled studies were at serious and five at critical risk of bias; all six uncontrolled studies were rated poor. Eryxin was added to other treatment in all but one arm. Favourable clinical and laboratory findings were reported, but interpretation was limited by confounding, incomplete reporting and, in some studies, differing co-interventions. Immunological findings varied across conditions and regimens without establishing a consistent response. Reporting gaps or inconsistencies were identified in 18 studies. Reported adverse events included transient taste or odour, flushing, tachycardia, fever and rash; ascertainment and denominators were inconsistent. Recorded certainty ratings were very low across conditions and for adverse events.Conclusions. The evidence does not establish effectiveness for any studied condition. This does not demonstrate absence of an effect. Overall and comparative safety remain uncertain. Well-conducted randomised controlled trials are needed to determine clinical benefits and harms.

paper_title: Electric Fields at the Blood–Brain Barrier: Electrochemotherapy and Electroporation-Based Therapies for Brain Tumors—A Narrative Review and Clinical Perspective
paper_abstract: The blood–brain barrier (BBB) limits systemic treatment of glioblastoma and brain metastases. Electroporation-based therapies apply short, high-intensity electric pulses that transiently permeabilize cell membranes or ablate tissue. Electrochemotherapy (ECT) combines reversible electroporation with chemotherapy, markedly enhancing bleomycin cytotoxicity, whereas irreversible electroporation (IRE) and its high-frequency variant (H-FIRE) induce non-thermal ablation and transiently disrupt the BBB in preclinical models. This narrative review critically examines the current evidence and identifies priorities for clinical translation. The available data remain predominantly preclinical. In rat gliomas, ECT delivered through a dedicated intracranial electrode achieved complete tumor eradication in 69% of treated animals, with effects largely confined to the target region. IRE and H-FIRE have proved technically feasible in dogs with spontaneous intracranial tumors, and H-FIRE has prolonged survival in rodent glioma models. Clinical experience is minimal: a non-invasive approach combining transcranial magnetic stimulation with bleomycin was withdrawn before patient enrollment, and the only identified trial of intracranial ECT for brain metastases was terminated for slow recruitment without published results. Major barriers include the lack of human safety and efficacy data, of intracranial electrodes approved for clinical use, and of validated treatment-planning workflows, together with uncertain recruitment feasibility. We also discuss how intracranial ECT might complement central nervous system (CNS)-active systemic therapies in patients with limited intracranial progression and controlled extracranial disease. Although most evidence derives from glioma models, we propose that selected patients with brain metastases recurring after stereotactic radiosurgery represent a rational population for initial pilot studies.

paper_title: The BASS Principle for Predictable Maxillary Sinus Bone Augmentation: A Conceptual Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Maxillary sinus floor elevation is common, yet newly formed bone remains unpredictable even when the Schneiderian membrane is intact and the immediate radiograph shows a well-shaped dome. Single-cause explanations do not account for this variability. Sinus augmentation differs from ridge augmentation: it creates a closed, air-filled, non-sterile compartment in which osteogenesis proceeds centripetally from the surrounding bony walls rather than from a vascularized defect bed. We therefore define the BASS principle, comprising Bone contact area, Angiogenesis, Stability of Space, and Safe healing. Bone contact area sets the osteogenic source and diffusion distance; angiogenesis sets the rate at which cells and nutrients reach the graft centre; stability of space preserves the container against intranasal pressure, graft resorption and micromotion; safe healing keeps it biologically undisturbed until mineralization is complete. The four domains are coupled, not additive: failure of any one is sufficient to make the outcome unpredictable. We map each domain onto measurable preoperative cone-beam computed tomography variables, intraoperative manoeuvres and recognizable failure phenotypes, and propose a workflow spanning case selection, surgical design and follow-up. BASS is a preventive design framework rather than a complication rescue algorithm; its thresholds require prospective validation.

paper_title: Investing Fascia–Carotid Sheath Mechanical Coupling Framework: A Mechanistic Narrative Review of Intravascular, Lymphatic, and Autonomic Neural Effects Within the Sheath
paper_abstract: Background and objective: The carotid sheath is a mechanical hub between superficial mechanical loads in the neck and deep neurovascular function. This article organizes the evidence at each node within the “investing fascia–carotid sheath mechanical coupling” framework, evaluates its evidence maturity and key gaps, and provides a testable node checklist for subsequent synchronized measurement studies.Methods: This article is a mechanistic narrative review. Literature inclusion used purposive sampling. PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched through October 31, 2026. No language restriction was applied, and the included literature was predominantly English, including one Chinese-language article. Inclusion criteria were provision of primary human evidence for the node, key animal functional evidence, methodological anchors, or key integrative reviews. Peer-reviewed original studies published online ahead of print were eligible, whereas preprints, conference abstracts, and unpublished registered trials were excluded. Standardized search and dual-reviewer screening procedures for systematic reviews were not used. Evidence maturity ratings were single-author integrative assessments based on study design and evidence type, without independent dual rating, and are not equivalent to risk-of-bias assessment in systematic reviews. An updated search will be performed before submission for literature published between October 31, 2026, and the submission date. If newly identified literature changes any node rating, this will be stated at revision.Key findings: Each node was supported by separate evidence, but causal connections between nodes have not been tested within the same study. The mechanical starting point involves both mechanical and biochemical molecular pathways, a cross-organ Piezo–ECM positive-feedback background, in vivo shear wave elastography (SWE) reliability, and direct measurements of pressure to the deep cervical fascia. However, the in vivo mechanical state of the investing fascia has not been linked to intrasheath variables. The arterial end has evidence of PIEZO functional necessity, human expression, ex vivo decomposition of wall–receptor responses, human electrical stimulation/mechanical compression intervention data, and a human quantitative precedent for transmission efficiency from external pressure to the carotid sinus; however, “fascial mechanical exposure–change in receptor function” has not been directly observed. The venous end has evidence of acute external compression sensitivity, improved flow after structural decompression, and observational associations in clinical populations; however, chronic fascial tension has not been covered, and the clinical associations are non-causal. The lymphatic node has human histological evidence, histopathological evidence, in vivo content load, animal functional resistance, dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI)/T1 mapping methodology, and drainage surrogate endpoints; neck lymph node dissection cohorts and animal mechanisms suggest that lymphatic structural injury can impair brain lymphatic clearance and synaptic protein homeostasis, but the exposure is not investing fascia mechanics. The sympathetic node has anatomical quantification, mechanical compression–induced changes in muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA), dose–response, and sham-controlled randomized controlled trial (RCT) evidence. However, the sign of the net effect of “sympathetic trunk compression–induced activation vs. baroreceptor compression–induced inhibition” remains uncertain. This node is rated moderate-to-high (molecular functional necessity limitedly satisfied); subtype definitions and thresholds are provided in Section 2 of the main text. The vagus node has anatomical variation, side-specific cross-sectional area (CSA) baseline, single-fiber recording methodology, and a same-individual structure–function pairing precedent; however, single-fiber activity has not been recorded under mechanical intervention. At the mechanotransduction level, there is evidence of PIEZO expression; however, functional activation under chronic mechanical exposure has not been tested in humans. In adjacent fields, a methodological precedent exists for same-individual joint analysis of “local tissue SWE + baroreflex function,” but the target was not the investing fascia. The seven node ratings are as follows: mechanical starting point, moderate; arterial end, moderate-to-high; venous end, moderate; lymphatic node, moderate; sympathetic node, moderate-to-high (molecular functional necessity limitedly satisfied); vagus node, moderate; and mechanotransduction, moderate-to-low. The direct intervention evidence status for the fascia–sheath interface in Section 3.8 is “preliminary”; it does not constitute an independent maturity level and does not participate in the seven-node rating.Conclusions: The evidence at each node separately supports different components of the framework, but causal connections between nodes have not yet been tested within the same study. Structural change and functional impairment may dissociate, the sign of the net sympathetic effect is uncertain, and the mechanistic rationale for deep cervical lymphatic–venous anastomosis (dcLVA) is questionable, constituting three competing explanations. The core gap is that “investing fascia mechanical state–intrasheath mechanical environment–target-structure functional marker” have never been synchronously measured in the same participant within the same time frame; this gap requires an answer from one or a group of multicenter studies using the same synchronized measurement paradigm. Several methodological anchors in the existing literature (e.g., the quantitative recording paradigm for transmission of external pressure to the carotid sinus, the directional difference between acute mechanical stimulation and chronic mechanical constraint, and the human feasibility of fascia–sheath interface intervention) can be reintegrated to support a synchronized measurement design, but they do not change the core gap judgment.

paper_title: Early Parenchymal FLAIR Hyperintensity and Hemorrhagic Transformation After Mechanical Thrombectomy: A Structured Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Background: Parenchymal fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) hyperintensity within an acute diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) lesion is a marker of ischemic tissue evolution, but whether it identifies patients at higher risk of hemorrhagic transformation after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is uncertain. Methods: We conducted a structured narrative review of cohort studies relating pretreatment lesion FLAIR signal to hemorrhage after reperfusion therapy. Four PubMed searches (1051 unique records) were supplemented by reference-list screening. Studies were classified by treatment, FLAIR construct and hemorrhage endpoint, and synthesized by direction and precision of effect without pooling. Results: Eleven cohort studies (49–412 patients each; 1726 in total) and one meta-analysis were included; four were MT or MT-predominant cohorts. The point estimate favored more hemorrhage with FLAIR positivity in nine studies. Associations were consistent for any hemorrhage, which is dominated by hemorrhagic infarction (59% vs. 39% in an MT cohort; odds ratio 20.0 in an intravenous-thrombolysis cohort imaged within 3 h). For parenchymal hematoma and symptomatic hemorrhage, three studies reported significant associations, whereas the largest MT cohort (n = 412) found no significant difference in parenchymal hematoma type 2 (10.7% vs. 6.8%, p = 0.193), and four further cohorts reported null or near-null estimates. No study isolated early-onset M1-occlusion patients with near-complete reperfusion. Conclusions: The evidence is directionally consistent but imprecise and does not show that FLAIR positivity independently predicts clinically important hemorrhage after MT. FLAIR positivity alone should not be used to withhold MT. Adequately powered studies with standardized FLAIR reading and separately reported parenchymal hematoma and symptomatic hemorrhage are needed.

paper_title: Heart Rate Variability for Longitudinal Monitoring in Professional Soccer Players: A Systematic Review of Prospective Observational Studies
paper_abstract: Background/Objectives: Heart rate variability (HRV) is widely used to monitor autonomic responses to training and match load in professional soccer, but the evidence is heterogeneous and its added value remains debated. This systematic review aimed to synthesize and critically appraise prospective longitudinal observational studies on HRV monitoring in male professional and semi-professional soccer players. Methods: The review followed PRISMA 2020 and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261533316). PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched from inception to September 2026. Two reviewers independently selected studies and extracted data; methodological quality was assessed with the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale (NOS). Owing to heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis was conducted. Results: After duplicate removal, 489 records were screened and eight studies (109 players; mean ages 18.7–26.6 years) were included: six during the competitive season and two during pre-season. NOS scores ranged from 6 to 8 out of 9, with confounder control as the main weakness. Time-domain vagal indices predominated (RMSSD in three studies, Ln-RMSSD in three). Reductions in RMSSD/Ln-RMSSD were associated with accumulated fatigue and high training loads, whereas increases in RMSSD and SD1 accompanied fitness gains during pre-season. RMSSD also related to match performance. One study linked an elevated LF/HF ratio to fatigue and muscle injury, although respiratory control was rarely reported. Conclusions: Short-term morning RMSSD/Ln-RMSSD, interpreted against individual baselines, appears the most consistent HRV marker, whereas spectral indices require cautious interpretation. Heterogeneity, small samples and limited confounder control prevent firm conclusions. Standardized protocols and multidimensional monitoring frameworks are needed.

paper_title: What Is Lost and What Is Gained When Psychiatric Care Moves from Physical to Digital Space? A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: The migration of psychiatric care from shared physical rooms to video, telephone and asynchronous platforms has been rapid, necessity-driven and unevenly evaluated. This narrative review, underpinned by structured searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, PsycINFO, Web of Science, Embase and the Cochrane Library with citation chasing, synthesises evidence on what is gained and what is lost when psychiatric care moves into digital space. Randomised and pooled evidence shows that telepsychiatric assessment, medication management and structured psychotherapy achieve outcomes comparable to in-person care; one meta-analysis found no difference in efficacy (standardised mean difference −0.01, 95% CI −0.12 to 0.09) or attrition (risk ratio 1.07, 95% CI 0.94–1.21). Gains cluster in reach, convenience, continuity, candour, reduced stigma and novel data streams such as passive sensing. Losses are consistent and reproducible: attenuated nonverbal and embodied information, loss of physical examination and psychomotor observation, lower clinician-rated alliance, erosion of the protected therapeutic setting, constrained crisis response, domestic privacy exposure, digital exclusion that amplifies inequity, documentation burden, videoconference fatigue, and fragmented licensure and prescribing frameworks. Apps, virtual reality and conversational agents add new therapeutic affordances, but with small-to-moderate effects and immature safety governance. Gains and losses are therefore asymmetrically distributed, and outcome equivalence is not experiential equivalence. We propose six design principles for hybrid care: treat modality as a shared clinical decision, preserve an embodied pathway, retrain communication, restore team-based workflow, make equity an explicit requirement, and govern digital tools with clinical rigour.

paper_title: Beyond the Degree: Determinants of Sustainable Research Careers and Scientific Publication After Postgraduate Education: A Critical Integrative Review with a Multilevel Action Framework and Implications for Latin America
paper_abstract: Postgraduate education has expanded faster than the posts and resources graduates need to keep a research career going, and the mismatch is sharpest in Latin America, where most researchers work in universities and investment in research and development (R&D) remains low. This critical in-tegrative review synthesizes evidence on the determinants of sustainable research careers and scientific publication after postgraduate education, builds a multilevel action framework from it and considers its implications for Latin America. A main search of Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection and ERIC (23 October 2026), complemented by a regional search of SciELO, LILACS and Redalyc (4 November 2026), retrieved 2,718 records. Deduplication, rule-based and title–abstract screening and full-text assessment left 62 studies published between 2015 and 2026, of which 28 were Latin American; a flow diagram adapted from PRISMA 2020 documents the selection. De-terminants were coded at individual, formative, organizational and systemic levels, and certainty was rated moderate only where two or more multivariable studies agreed. No common measure of research continuity exists, and productivity and well-being are rarely examined together. Organi-zational conditions carry the most consistent evidence: postdoctoral positions and institutional mobility ease access to academic posts, while protected time and early funding each depend on a single study. Doctoral publication predicts later trajectories only modestly. Gender gaps arise in early productivity, type of position, funding access and promotion, yet they weaken once organi-zational resources are taken into account. In Latin America, boundary conditions include the con-centration of jobs in universities and public bodies, cycles of public funding, national evaluation requirements and support networks on return, and most regional evidence is descriptive. The re-view proposes six propositions and eleven action levers, beginning with systematic graduate tracking, consistent with Sustainable Development Goal target 9.5.

paper_title: The Gifts We Give: A Transdisciplinary Narrative Review of Longitudinal Treatment, Epigenetic Regulation, and Intergenerational Risk in Bipolar Disorder
paper_abstract: Background: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a highly heritable and clinically heterogeneous psychiatric condition whose expression reflects interactions among polygenic liability, illness course, treatment, physical health, and environmental context. Epigenetic mechanisms—including DNA methylation, histone modification, chromatin regulation, and non-coding RNAs—are relevant to gene regulation in BD, but current human evidence does not establish that treatment-associated epigenetic changes are biologically transmitted to offspring. Objectives: This transdisciplinary narrative review examines whether longitudinal pharmacological and psychosocial treatment influences epigenetic processes within individuals with BD and considers the implications of these treatment-associated processes for intergenerational risk and resilience. Methods: A targeted, iterative search of HOLLIS, Google Scholar, and PubMed/MEDLINE prioritized peer-reviewed publications from January 2020 through August 2026, supplemented by backward and selective forward citation searching and foundational earlier studies. Results: Pharmacological treatments, including lithium and valproate, influence molecular and gene-regulatory pathways, although BD-specific longitudinal epigenetic evidence remains preliminary and heterogeneous. Psychological interventions have established clinical and functional benefits, but direct evidence of durable epigenetic modification in BD remains insufficient. Overall, treatment-associated biological and contextual modulation within individuals is better supported than germline epigenetic transmission. Conclusions: Future prospective, repeated-measures, parent–offspring, and multigenerational studies are needed to distinguish treatment effects from inherited genetic liability, illness state, prenatal exposure, shared environment, caregiving, and true transgenerational inheritance.

paper_title: Anode Materials, Conductive Coatings, and Prestressing Steel in Cathodic Protection of Concrete Structures: A Critical Review of Properties, Degradation, and Safety
paper_abstract: The durability and safety of cathodic protection (CP) in reinforced and prestressed concrete depend on interactions among electrode materials, electrochemical conditions, and structural response. This critical review examines how anode composition, microstructure, conductive layers, concrete resistivity, and current distribution affect protection performance and material degradation. Laboratory studies, numerical simulations, and field evidence are compared for titanium/mixed-metal-oxide anodes, zinc-based galvanic systems, graphite and carbon-modified cementitious materials, polymeric coatings, and contact mortars. Particular attention is paid to interfacial processes, distinguishing initial conductivity and current delivery from electrochemical stability, anode consumption, and demonstrated service life. Accelerated aging and field exposure are treated as complementary, but non-equivalent, evidence of durability. For prestressing steel, the effects of cathodic polarization, strength, stress state, and exposure on hydrogen-assisted damage are examined; meeting protection criteria alone does not establish hydrogen safety. Instant-off potentials, depolarization measurements, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy are assessed alongside material and structural diagnostics, including their limitations. A three-dimensional P–T–B framework distinguishes local protection performance (P), technological durability (T), and material and structural safety (B). Standardized characterization and long-term validation remain necessary before laboratory findings can inform prestressed-concrete applications under realistic operating and environmental exposure conditions.

paper_title: Offsite and Modular Construction for Saudi Giga-Projects and Housing Delivery: A Review of Drivers, Barriers and Enablers, and a Design-Led Readiness Maturity Model
paper_abstract: Saudi Arabia is trying to deliver housing and giga-project accommodation at a pace that conventional wet construction struggles to sustain. The Ministry of Municipalities and Housing has set a target of 40% of new houses built with modern methods of construction (MMC) by 2030, and its Modern Building Initiative supports six MMC technologies and has financed more than 22 factories. Yet the peer-reviewed evidence on how offsite, modular and prefabricated construction performs in Saudi conditions is thin and scattered. This review brings together Saudi and Gulf empirical studies (surveys, case studies, economic modelling and risk analyses) with the main international reviews on modular integrated construction (MiC), prefabrication and design for manufacture and assembly (DfMA). A scoping search in OpenAlex on 6 November 2026 returned 38 records for Saudi-specific offsite terms, of which only eight dealt with building offsite construction on title screening; targeted searches and citation tracking raised the final base to 37 peer-reviewed sources, supported by 13 official and industry sources for policy facts. The evidence shows that speed, labour dependence and quality drive interest, while cost, late design freeze, supply-chain gaps, transport limits, regulatory routes, skills and a strong preference for traditional methods hold adoption back. The Saudi studies repeat the international pattern, but with two local features: very high reliance on expatriate site labour and a policy push that is ahead of design practice. The paper proposes the Saudi Offsite Readiness Model (SORM), with seven dimensions, five maturity levels, 28 measurable indicators, a weakest-link scoring rule and a stage-by-stage checklist written for architects. A research agenda closes the paper.

paper_title: A Survey of Self-Evolving Embodied Agents: On the Path to Real-World Physical Intelligence
paper_abstract: Embodied artificial intelligence is moving beyond static task execution toward agents that can continuously adapt, learn, and improve through physical interaction with the world. While recent advances in large language models, vision-language models, robotic foundation models, vision-language-action models, and world models have significantly enhanced the perception, reasoning, and action capabilities of embodied agents, most existing systems remain constrained by offline training, fixed policies, and limited post-deployment adaptability. This survey investigates self-evolving embodied agents as an emerging research agenda for advancing toward real-world physical intelligence. We define self-evolution as the capability of embodied agents to accumulate experience, detect and correct errors, update memory, policies, skills, and models, and expand their capability boundaries through long-term interaction. To make the review auditable, we specify the literature scope, inclusion criteria, evidence types, and coding rules used in the comparative tables. We first clarify the conceptual foundations of self-evolving embodied agents and distinguish them from related paradigms such as test-time adaptation, online learning, continual learning, and lifelong learning. We then propose a unified closed-loop framework consisting of perception, state representation, memory, reasoning and planning, action, feedback, reflection, and evolution. Based on this framework, we review the historical progression from classical robotics and offline embodied learning to embodied foundation models, interactive adaptation, and self-evolving agents. We further summarize key mechanisms supporting self-evolution, including data and experience acquisition, memory-centric learning, world-modeldriven prediction, feedback-based reflection, policy and skill evolution, multi-agent co-evolution, and safety-aligned updating. Finally, we discuss representative tasks, benchmarks, evaluation protocols, open challenges, and future directions. This survey argues that self-evolution is a necessary but still weakly evidenced step toward embodied agents that can safely, autonomously, and continually grow in open-ended real-world environments.

paper_title: Intelligent Healthcare: A Systematic Review of Digital Twins in Healthcare Systems
paper_abstract: Digital twins (DTs) have emerged as a transformative technology across various industries, and their potential in healthcare is garnering significant attention. DTs represent digital replicas of physical objects, systems, processes, and environments, offering unprecedented opportunities for personalized, precision, and intelligent healthcare. This paper systematically reviews the current applications of DTs in healthcare, focusing on how these technologies can enhance healthcare, improve patient and provider experiences, and deliver intelligent and personalized care. By leveraging immersive virtual worlds, healthcare practitioners can simulate complex medical situations, refine treatment strategies, and engage patients in more tailored, interactive ways. However, the integration of DTs into healthcare systems also presents technical, regulatory, and ethical challenges, such as data privacy concerns, the need for standardized protocols, and issues of accessibility. Addressing these challenges is crucial for the successful adoption and implementation of DTs in healthcare. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the transformative potential of DTs in intelligent healthcare, while also highlighting the need for continued research and development in this rapidly evolving field. Through this systematic review, we seek to encourage further innovation and collaboration, paving the way for a future where DTs play a central role in intelligent healthcare delivery.

paper_title: Measuring Agreement Between AI and the Radiologist: A Methodological Review of Evaluation Metrics for Study-Level Concordance in Real-World, Whole-Study CT and MRI
paper_abstract: As multimodal large language models (LLMs) are applied to computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), how agreement between an artificial intelligence (AI) system and the radiologist is measured determines whether reported progress is believable. This structured narrative review maps the metric families for AI–radiologist concordance on CT/MRI reports and assesses each against a demanding setting: whole-study analysis of real-world data, where an individual submits a single study without priors, laboratory data or indication, and the radiologist report is an imperfect, non-exhaustive reference, a premise anchored in the radiologist discrepancy literature. We reviewed lexical, clinical/factuality, composite and LLM-as-judge metrics; inter-rater agreement statistics (the kappa family, Gwet’s AC1, PABAK, Krippendorff’s alpha, intraclass correlation) and the unit of agreement each presupposes; LLM-as-judge biases; and reporting standards. Entity-based and LLM-as-judge metrics with explicit error taxonomies align best with radiologist judgement but require validation. A worked example shows Cohen’s and Fleiss’ kappa collapsing under the class imbalance typical of findings data; prevalence-robust coefficients are more trustworthy, and Fleiss’ kappa belongs to multi-reader panel reliability, not AI-versus-report concordance. We recommend a layered metric stack anchored on significance-tiered finding recall, computed by an LLM judge validated as non-inferior to human–human agreement, and reported under CLAIM 2024, STARD-AI and TRIPOD-LLM.

paper_title: Deciding Without Generating: A Survey of Typed Decision Models, from Jev to Open Decision LLMs
paper_abstract: Many applications of large language models need a decision rather than free text. Examples include assigning a category, giving a score, answering yes or no, or choosing the next action. Prior work has used language models for such decisions in several ways, including zero-shot classification, reward models and verifiers, LLM-as-a-Judge, safety classifiers, and model cascades. In most of these approaches, the model generates text, and the decision must then be extracted from it. Recently, a class of models has emerged that answers typed questions directly, without generating text. Given an input and a set of questions with predefined answer types, such a model returns, for each question, an answer in the declared format together with probabilities over the possible answers, and for some question types a confidence score. We call these models typed decision models. The commercial model Jev made this design widely known, and it was soon followed by many open models and by similar services from other providers. Research on typed decision models is growing quickly but is scattered across many communities. This survey reviews the area. We trace its roots in earlier work and give a formal description of typed decision models whose outputs depend on the question type. We analyze how these models are combined with stronger fallback models, and show that such a combination improves accuracy only if the fallback corrects more errors than it introduces on the inputs passed to it. We then review model designs, training methods, sources of efficiency, applications, benchmarks, and known failure modes. In the reported settings, typed decision models are often much faster and cheaper than generative models, and they are often competitive on tasks where the needed evidence is stated in the input. They tend to perform worse on tasks that require multi-step reasoning and against supervised models trained on in-domain data. Their probabilities also depend on how a question is asked, and they can be misled by option names and by untrusted input. We conclude with open problems for future research.

paper_title: Bariatric Surgery and Colorectal Cancer Risk: A Critical Narrative Review of Comparative Evidence and Clinical Implications
paper_abstract: Bariatric surgery is often presented as cancer-preventive, but its association with colorectal cancer (CRC) is less clear than for other obesity-related cancers. This critical narrative review examined epidemiological studies, evidence syntheses, human mechanistic studies and guidance identified through targeted searches updated to 31 October 2026, separating comparisons with nonsurgical obesity care from comparisons with the general population. Most meta-analyses report inverse associations, but results depend on the estimator and study selection: two largely overlapping reviews reported a nonsignificant pooled hazard ratio (HR) of 0.88 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.69–1.12), and HRs of 0.81 and 0.75 only after excluding one study. Persistent excess colon cancer risk relative to the general population does not by itself indicate harm from surgery. The Swedish Obese Subjects study found no significant adjusted association after a median 22.2 years, and an October 2026 Nordic cohort found none for colon or rectal cancer. Human mucosal findings diverge, and experimental data offer hypotheses rather than clinical proof. The magnitude and causality of any association remain uncertain, and no late postoperative hazard is established. Screening after surgery should follow established risk factors, prior colonoscopy findings and symptoms rather than the operation alone.

paper_title: Measuring Psychological Defense: Reliability, Convergent Validity, and Evidence for Causal Mechanisms—A Scoping Review
paper_abstract: Background: Psychological defenses are central to psychodynamic theory, yet their measurement spans distinct observational, projective, self-report, and computational traditions. Whether these methods identify comparable constructs—and whether reliably classified defense patterns constitute distinct causal mechanisms—remains uncertain. Objective: To map the measurement of psychological defense across levels of aggregation; evaluate evidence on inter-rater reliability and convergence between methods; and characterize experimental, formal-modeling, and multichannel approaches to mechanistic validation. Methods: This scoping review followed JBI guidance and was reported with reference to PRISMA-ScR. OpenAlex and PubMed were searched on October 4, 2026, supplemented by one-step forward and backward citation searching. Of 7,902 records identified, 6,375 unique records were screened and 348 were included in the evidence map; 112 full texts were examined. A second assessor independently screened a random sample of 300 records (Cohen κ = 0.63; 95% CI, 0.42–0.79). Descriptive summaries were based on 78 eligible human–human agreement coefficients from 19 sources, selected from a broader chart of reliability estimates. Results: Inter-rater agreement varied across measurement units, instruments, materials, and procedures. The reported median agreement was 0.78 for individual defenses measured from standardized projective or narrative stimuli (23 coefficients), 0.43 for sets of individual defenses predominantly coded from interviews or speech (12 coefficients), 0.70 for defense levels (22 coefficients), 0.74 for styles or summary scales (6 coefficients), and 0.75 for overall defensive functioning (15 coefficients). These descriptive medians are not directly comparable because coefficient types and study conditions differed. Individual Defense Style Questionnaire scales showed variable internal consistency (median Cronbach α = 0.46 across 21 defenses in one sample). Evidence of convergence between independent methods at the individual-defense level was limited. The map identified 22 experimental records and 16 multichannel studies, but no study meeting the review’s proposed criterion for independent, episode-level confirmation across speech, subjective experience, and physiology. Conclusions: Broad indicators of defensive functioning are measured with reasonable reproducibility in several research settings, whereas evidence for consistently identifying particular defenses in naturalistic material is more dependent on measurement design. Current findings cannot determine whether this reflects limitations of instruments, context-dependent expression, or the construct structure itself. Progress requires within-sample comparisons across measurement units, independent-method validation, and preregistered experimental tests of specific causal predictions.

paper_title: Agentic Chip Design: A Survey of Architectures, Design Methodologies, and Evaluation
paper_abstract: Agentic chip design combines large language models with electronic design automation (EDA) tools to plan, execute, and revise design operations. Its effectiveness depends on how an agent translates requirements into executable tasks, interprets diagnostic information, and coordinates changes across design stages. This survey examines these relationships across digital design, agent architectures, EDA algorithm and tool development, and evaluation, with additional coverage of analog, mixed-signal, and radio-frequency applications. We compare agentic chip-design methods through the design representations they modify, the feedback used to select revisions, and the procedures used to check correctness and implementation quality. The analysis shows that broader agent control over designs and EDA software expands optimization opportunities while increasing the need to manage dependencies and verify changes across the design flow. We also compare benchmarks and evaluation methods, focusing on functional correctness, implementation quality, and computational cost. These comparisons identify research directions in specification interpretation, failure diagnosis, repository-level integration, cross-stage optimization, and efficient tool use. By synthesizing these findings, this survey aims to guide the research community in developing and evaluating more reliable and efficient chip-design agents.

paper_title: What do Patients Wish Their Psychiatrist Had Asked—But Never Asked? A Narrative Review of the Unspoken Agenda in Psychiatric Consultations
paper_abstract: Objective: To synthesise evidence on what patients wish their psychiatrist had asked but did not, why these questions go unasked, what follows from the silence, and which interventions close the gap. Methods: Narrative review, reported against the SANRA scale, of literature identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, the Cochrane Library and Google Scholar to November 2025, integrating conversation-analytic and observational studies, service-user surveys and qualitative research, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, and randomised trials. Results: Evidence converged on eight domains: medication purpose and exit; sexual function; physical health and weight; suicidal thoughts; trauma; work, money and company; identity and stigma; and how information and decisions are handled. The gap is measurable. The patient's preferred approach to receiving information was rated at the lowest possible level in 80 of 80 recorded consultations; 34% of service users reported being offered a choice of medication, whereas 57% of clinicians believed they always or nearly always offered one; sexual dysfunction was detected in 58% of patients on direct questioning but 14% spontaneously; and 70% of patients concealing suicidal ideation feared practical consequences, chiefly hospitalisation. Five mechanisms suppress enquiry: disconfirming question design, divergent agendas, power and prior coercion, stigma, and time pressure that is largely perceived. Structured consultations, question prompt lists, decision aids, specific clinician training, trauma-informed enquiry and routine outcome monitoring have supporting evidence. Conclusion: The unasked question is a systematic, measurable and clinically consequential feature of psychiatric practice, linked to concealed risk, non-adherence, unmet need and disengagement. The deficit is one of implementation, not knowledge. Practice implications: Psychiatrists should replace disconfirming questions with open invitations, ask every patient how they want information and decisions handled, enquire routinely across the eight domains, make the consequences of disclosing suicidal thoughts transparent, and embed structured patient-agenda tools in routine care.

paper_title: Deep Learning Theory through the Lens of Statistical Physics: A Topical Review
paper_abstract: The recent success of foundation models and deep learning has far outpaced our theoretical understanding of how large-scale neural networks learn and generalize. Statistical physics provides a natural language for describing such high-dimensional, nonlinear, and strongly coupled systems, offering concepts such as mean-field theory, phase transitions, energy landscapes, and stochastic dynamics. In this topical review, we adopt a statistical-physics way of thinking -- from concepts including phases and criticality, and free-energy viewpoints, to methods such as kernel and Gaussian-process limits, mean-field and dynamical mean-field theories, random-matrix tools, and Fokker-Planck formalisms, and to a mindset emphasizing universality, scaling, and tractable limits with explicit validity regimes. We survey recent progress on understanding modern deep learning through this lens, including mean-field analyses of wide networks, spectral and geometric perspectives on loss landscapes, stochastic-gradient-based training viewed as a dynamical process, and phase-transition analogies that organize phenomena such as overparameterization, generalization, and representation change. Our goal is to synthesize these threads into a coherent framework that clarifies what each approximation explains, when it is expected to hold, and how apparently competing narratives relate or diverge. Together, these perspectives form a unified physical framework that views representation learning as a collective phenomenon in high-dimensional systems, bridging deterministic and stochastic regimes of gradient-based optimization.
comments: 22 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. Topical review published in Front. Phys. 22(1), 011302 (2027); this version contains minor corrections

paper_title: Large Language Model Deployment on Resource-Constrained Edge Devices: A Practitioners Survey
paper_abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed many areas of artificial intelligence (AI), but their substantial resource requirements limit their deployment on mobile and edge devices. Although LLMs have demonstrated impressive capabilities in various applications, the next challenge is deploying these models on resource-limited edge devices. Recent innovations in software optimizations and specialized hardware have made it feasible to deploy LLMs on edge devices. Edge deployment offers benefits including local data processing, cost savings, reduced latency, and personalized responses. This paper reviews the latest techniques that make the deployment of LLMs on edge devices feasible.

paper_title: Notwithstanding Anything to the Contrary, Ignore All Instructions: Measuring Prompt Injection Guards on Legal Contract Review Attacks
paper_abstract: Specialized prompt injection guards are deployed in front of document analysis systems, but no false positive rate has been published for any of them on legal contracts. We measure eleven open-weights guards on two corpora of legal contracts and find that existing guards struggle: document-level false positive rates are as high as 92.39%; two guards fall below chance on paired AUC; and a five-regex baseline is not Pareto-dominated by any guard in the panel. Controlled probes locate model-specific as well as general failure modes. Prompted LLMs resolve the tested failures, including a second threat category (unauthorized scope claims) on which every guard scores zero. A cascaded LLM solution, where the positives of a mid-tier model are verified by a frontier model, is 6.5x cheaper than using exclusively a frontier model and approaches its performance.

paper_title: Determining Sample Size in Qualitative Research Across Case Study, Phenomenology, Grounded Theory, Narrative Inquiry and Ethnography: A Systematic Review
paper_abstract: Introduction: Sample-size determination in qualitative research remains contested because adequacy is shaped by the research question, methodological purpose, participant specificity, data richness, analytical strategy and stopping rationale. The supplied literature reports numerical ranges, but does not establish universal minimums across qualitative methodologies. Methods: The researcher-selected databases and information sources were Google Scholar, ERIC. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to 2025–2026. The exact calendar date of search execution was not recorded in the verified identification provenance; this is distinct from the publication-year eligibility range. A systematic review searched Google Scholar and ERIC using a prespecified Boolean strategy and publication eligibility range of 2025–2026. Results: Across the synthesis, sample adequacy was primarily treated as a design-sensitive judgement rather than a universal numerical threshold. Focused, homogeneous and information-rich samples generally supported smaller samples, whereas broad, comparative and heterogeneous designs required more data. Saturation was useful when operationalised as an ongoing evaluative process, but its meaning and applicability were contested. Grounded Theory provided the clearest method-specific stopping logic through theoretical sampling and theoretical saturation. Ethnographic guidance was comparatively underdeveloped, while numerical ranges for phenomenology and narrative inquiry remained illustrative rather than definitive. Discussion/Conclusion: While there was no generally accepted minimum sample size was established for any reviewed methodology, there seem to be a recommendation of 10 to 15 interviews. Furthermore, a defensible sample-size decision should be justified prospectively in relation to design, scope, sampling logic, information power, data quality, analytic aims and an explicitly documented stopping assessment.

paper_title: Quality and Authenticity Evaluation of Condiments Using Near-Infrared Spectroscopy: A Critical Review
paper_abstract: Condiment matrices are chemically complex, and seasonings of different categories suffer from batch-to-batch variations and high risks of adulteration. Conventional physicochemical titration and chromatographic methods involved laborious sample pretreatment and long assay durations, which hindered their applications for on-line production monitoring and large-scale commodity screening. Combined with chemometrics, near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) had enabled rapid, non-destructive and simultaneous multi-parameter analysis, and had emerged as a vital tool for condiment quality assessment. This review had systematically summarized research advances of NIRS in condiment analysis, covering quantitative determination of physicochemical properties, authentication and adulteration detection, geographical origin tracing, and on-line monitoring of fermentation processes. Key bottlenecks restricting industrial implementation had been discussed, including spectral overlap interferences derived from complex matrices, limited sensitivity toward trace constituents, poor model transferability across instruments, and the absence of unified industrial standards and shared spectral libraries. Prospects had been proposed from the perspectives of multi-modal data fusion, spectral interpretation algorithms, full-supply-chain quality traceability, and standardization, providing theoretical support and references for the technical upgrading and large-scale industrial implementation of rapid condiment detection.

paper_title: Generative AI and Cognitive Processes in Education: A Narrative Review and Conceptual Framework
paper_abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly being integrated into educational practices, transforming how students access information, develop ideas, and carry out cognitive tasks. While GenAI offers opportunities to foster critical thinking and creativity, its use raises concerns regarding "cognitive offloading"—the delegation of reasoning processes that are fundamental to learning. This study presents a review based on 108 documents from Scopus and Web of Science, which allowed for an examination of the relationships between GenAI, critical thinking, creativity, and cognitive offloading, as well as their pedagogical and institutional implications. The evidence analyzed suggests that GenAI can improve immediate task performance, facilitate idea generation, and support content development. However, these benefits do not necessarily translate into autonomous learning or greater creative originality. Outcomes appear to depend on students' prior knowledge, their AI literacy, task design, metacognitive regulation, and the nature and timing of pedagogical support. Based on this review, an AI-Mediated Cognitive Infrastructure Framework (AMCIF) is proposed, which links GenAI usage patterns with cognitive processes, educational practices, and institutional conditions. This framework distinguishes between forms of assistance that promote cognitive engagement and those that might replace the mental activity necessary for learning, emphasizing the essential role of instructor mediation, source verification, reflective practices, and process-oriented assessment. The AMCIF provides a conceptual foundation for analyzing how to integrate GenAI into educational settings while preserving critical judgment, creativity, and the capacity for independent reasoning. The proposed relationships require rigorous empirical validation.

paper_title: Beyond Animal Models: A Comprehensive Review of In Vitro, In Silico, and Organ-on-Chip Methods for Assessing Pharmacological Safety and Effectiveness
paper_abstract: Background: Traditional animal models in preclinical pharmacology show limited predictive accuracy for human outcomes due to interspecies differences, contributing to high drug attrition rates and ethical concerns. Recent regulatory changes have pushed the development of alternative, human-centered methods.Objective: To comprehensively investigate and evaluate novel non-animal approaches for establishing pharmacological safety and efficacy, such as organ-on-a-chip technologies, in vitro systems, and in silico models.Methods: A narrative evaluation of existing literature was conducted, concentrating on the technological principles, pharmacological applications, predictive performance, and regulatory acceptance of alternative testing strategies.Results: Compared with traditional 2D cultures, advanced in vitro models such as 3D organoids and iPSC-derived cells exhibit greater physiological relevance. Rapid, economical, and high-throughput predictions are made possible by in silico methods such as QSAR, PBPK modeling, and AI-based technologies. With improved translational fidelity, organ-on-a-chip technologies mimic the dynamic microenvironments of human organs. Strong, mechanism-based safety assessment frameworks are produced by integrated testing procedures that combine these methods. But there are still issues with scalability, validation, and standards.Conclusion: With growing regulatory approval for their future application, the incorporation of alternative approaches signifies a paradigm change toward more ethical, human-centered, and predictive drug development.

paper_title: A Structured Review of Distributed Quantum Computing: Infrastructure, Protocols, Applications, Compilation, and Security
paper_abstract: Distributed quantum computing (DQC) connects quantum processing units (QPUs) to execute programs beyond the capacity of a single processor. Understanding its scalability requires examining the interactions between hardware, communication, software, and security. This structured review synthesizes 126 studies, mainly published between 2020 and 2026 with foundational earlier work, retrieved from eight sources and selected using documented inclusion and exclusion criteria. We organize the literature into five pillars: infrastructure, protocols, applications, compilation, and security. A common scoping rule distinguishes work enabling distributed computation from broader quantum communication research. The synthesis identifies interconnect rate and fidelity, classical control latency, remote-operation overhead, and coherence constraints as coupled limits on distributed execution. Infrastructure and protocol research includes experimental demonstrations, whereas application and compiler evaluations remain predominantly simulation-based. Security requires both protected interconnects and confidential, verifiable delegated computation. Comparisons across the pillars reveal tradeoffs between local computation, communication resources, sampling overhead, and trust assumptions. The review highlights unresolved challenges in distributed fault tolerance, transduction, interoperable software, benchmarking, and integrated security. Its central conclusion is that scalable DQC requires coordinated hardware–software–network design and evaluation of complete systems rather than isolated improvements within individual layers.

paper_title: Iron Supplementation in Early Childhood and the Spectrum of Neurocognitive Development: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
paper_abstract: Introduction: Iron deficiency during pregnancy and early childhood may affect myelination, neurotransmission, and neural network maturation, with potential consequences for motor, cognitive, and language development. Objective: To quantitatively synthesize the effects of iron supplementation on motor, cognitive/global, and language development by integrating the original dataset with a complementary search for original studies. Methods: Systematic review with random-effects quantitative synthesis. The expanded review included 11 publications.
